title: Nouns, Gender & “the”
summary: The definite article ال, sun and moon letters, and feminine ة.

sections.body: Arabic has no separate word for “a”. A plain noun already means “a”: بَيْت bayt = a house. Add ال to the front to make it “the”: الْبَيْت al-bayt = the house.
Before half the alphabet, the l of al- is pronounced. Before the other half, it disappears and the next letter is doubled instead. The names come from the two classic examples:

rows: sun letter: l is silent, sh is doubled

sections.body: The 14 sun letters are ت ث د ذ ر ز س ش ص ض ط ظ ل ن. Every other letter is a moon letter. Tip: sun letters are all made with the tip of the tongue.
Every noun is masculine or feminine. Most feminine nouns end in tāʼ marbūṭa ة, pronounced -a: مَدْرَسَة madrasa (school), سَيَّارَة sayyāra (car). A few feminine words don't, like شَمْس (sun).
